title_ar: الاقتراض من البنك الربوي لأجل الزواج
title_en: Borrowing from an Interest-Based Bank for the Sake of Marriage
body_ar:
أنا شاب مقدم على الزواج فهل يجوز لي أن أقترض من البنك وأنا موظف للدولة في مجال التعليم ؟

الجواب أن القرض الربوي لا يحل للإنسان إلا إذا اضطر له فإن الله تعالى يقول: " يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقو الله وذرو ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين، ويقول تعالى " يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تأكلوا الربا أضعافا مضاعفة واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون واتقوا النار التي أعدت للكافرين"، فلا يحل للإنسان الإقدام على أخذ القرض الربوي إلا مضطرا والضرورة مثل أن يخاف على نفسه الزنا وأن لا يجد ما يدفعه مهرا ، وهنا نصيحة للشباب أن كثيرا من الناس يظن أن الزواج له تكاليف كبيرة وأنه لا يمكن أن يقدم عليه إلا إذا جمع أموالا طائلة فخير الأنكحة أقلها تكاليفا وخير النساء أقلهن مهرا ، وقد ثبت في حديث ابن عباس " أن أفضل هذه الأمة أقلها صداقا، وثبت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال عليكم خير النساء صلح نساء قريش؛ أحناه على ولد في صغره، وأرعاه على زوج في ذات يده وأرضاه بالقليل، فإذا اضطر الإنسان ولم يجد ما يكون صداقا مع أنه لم يكن يأتي بسرف ولا بخيلة ولم يجد من يقرضه ولا من يتاجر معه بدين، فحينئذ تكون حالته يمكن أن تنزل منزل الضرورة وتحتاج إلى استفتاء خاص ممن يطلع على ظروفه وشؤونه وهل هو صاحب رخصة أم لا .
body_en:
I am a young man about to marry. Is it permissible for me to take a loan from the bank, being a state employee in the field of education?

The answer is that the usurious loan is not lawful for a person unless he is under necessity (ḍarūrah) with respect to it. For God, exalted, says: 'O you who believe, be conscious of God and give up what remains of usurious gain (ribā), if you are believers.' And He says, exalted: 'O you who believe, do not consume usurious gain, doubled and multiplied; and be conscious of God, that you may prosper. And guard yourselves against the Fire, which has been prepared for the disbelievers.' So it is not lawful for a person to go ahead and take the usurious loan except under necessity; and necessity is, for instance, that he fears fornication for himself and finds nothing to pay as the bridal gift (mahr).

And here is a piece of counsel for young men. Many people suppose that marriage has great costs, and that they cannot go ahead with it unless they have gathered enormous sums. But the best of marriages is the one with the least cost, and the best of women is the one whose bridal gift is least. It is established in the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas that 'the best of this community is the one whose marriage payment is least'. And it is established from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: 'Take to yourselves the best of women — the virtuous women of Quraysh: the most tender of them towards a child in its infancy, and the most careful of them over a husband in respect of what his hand possesses, and the most content of them with little.'

So if a person is under necessity and finds nothing to serve as the marriage payment — while not being one who goes to extravagance or ostentation — and finds no one to lend to him and no one to trade with him on credit, then at that point his situation is one that can be brought down to the standing of necessity. And it requires a fatwa of its own from someone who is acquainted with his circumstances and his affairs, and whether he qualifies for the dispensation (rukhṣah) or not.

flags.arabic: وتحتاج إلى استفتاء خاص ممن يطلع على ظروفه وشؤونه وهل هو صاحب رخصة أم لا
flags.context: the final sentence of the answer
options: render faithfully and mark that the Sheikh expressly declines to settle the case
present the answer as a permission to borrow under these conditions
present the answer as a refusal
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The Sheikh does not answer this questioner's case. He sets out the general rule that a usurious loan is unlawful except under necessity, describes what could amount to necessity, and then explicitly refers the man to a separate fatwa from someone who knows his actual circumstances and can judge whether he qualifies for the dispensation. He never says whether this young man may borrow. An English reader, and especially one looking for a permission, will take the description of necessity for a grant of it. This must not be displayed as a ruling that borrowing for marriage is permitted.

flags.arabic: والضرورة مثل أن يخاف على نفسه الزنا
flags.context: the example the Sheikh gives of what could constitute necessity
options: render literally, as one example among possible cases
render as the definition of necessity in this matter
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW, AND A THRESHOLD FLAG. The glossary is explicit that ḍarūrah is a technical threshold and not general hardship, and that ḥājah is a lower threshold with different legal effect. The Sheikh gives a single illustrative example introduced by mithl, 'such as', and the English must keep it as an example and not let it become the test. The example itself — fear of fornication — is blunt in English and sits in a record about bank borrowing, which is a combination that reads awkwardly out of context. Translated faithfully; the publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.arabic: عليكم خير النساء صلح نساء قريش
options: read صلح as صالح and render 'the virtuous women of Quraysh'
read as ṣaluḥa, a verb, and render 'the women of Quraysh have proved good'
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. صلح as printed will not construe. The attested wording of this report is khayr nisāʾ rakibna al-ibil ṣāliḥu nisāʾ Quraysh, so صالح is the evident reading and a letter has dropped. The source spelling is preserved in body_ar; the English takes the likely reading. Note too that the Sheikh's quotation compresses the report and drops its opening clause about riding camels. Nothing has been restored.

flags.arabic: مع أنه لم يكن يأتي بسرف ولا بخيلة
flags.context: the qualification on the person who finds nothing to pay
options: while not being one who goes to extravagance or ostentation (reading مخيلة)
while not being extravagant or miserly (reading بخيلة, 'miserly')
flags.note: GENUINELY AMBIGUOUS, AND IT MATTERS. بخيلة as printed can be read either as bi-khīlah, 'with ostentation' — which pairs naturally with saraf, extravagance, and fits the Sheikh's counsel against inflated wedding costs — or as bakhīlah, 'miserly', which would pair oddly with extravagance but is the more obvious reading of the letters. The first reading has been taken in the body because it fits the argument, but the choice is not secure and a reviewer should settle it.

The glossary is explicit that 'interest' is to be avoided for ribā because the category is wider than interest. 'Usurious gain' has been used for the noun and 'usurious loan' for al-qarḍ al-ribawī. The title of the record uses 'interest-based bank' only because that is how such an institution is named in English; the body keeps the glossary rendering throughout.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-27 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The two Qur'anic citations are given in the source between straight quotation marks, with the opening mark of the first never closed before the second begins; the defect is preserved in body_ar. The wordings match Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:278 and Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:130–131. The source also spells اتقو and ذرو without the final alif.

'Marriage payment' renders ṣadāq and 'bridal gift' renders mahr; the Sheikh uses both words for the same thing and the English keeps them distinct only so that the reader can see which word he used where. The glossary's caution against 'dowry' applies to both.

The Sheikh says of the Ibn ʿAbbas report only that it is 'established' (thābit) and names no collection; for the second report he says it is established from the Prophet. Both attributions are reproduced exactly as he gives them and no grading has been added.
